blocks.text: Anthropic 的新模型 Fable 5.2 在 Remote Labor Index 上实现大幅跃升，以专业水准完成了超过 41% 的真实自由职业项目。这一成绩把它的上一代模型和所有竞争对手都远远甩在身后。

inlines.text: Anthropic 的新模型 Fable 5.2 在 Remote Labor Index 上实现大幅跃升，以专业水准完成了超过 41% 的真实自由职业项目。这一成绩把它的上一代模型和所有竞争对手都远远甩在身后。

blocks.text: 在 Scale Labs 与人工智能安全中心（CAIS）推出的 Remote Labor Index（RLI） 上，Anthropic 的新模型 Fable 5.2 以 41.3% 的成绩领跑。该测试衡量的是 AI 智能体完成真实自由职业工作、且质量足以让付费客户接受的比例。

blocks.text: 这一进展说明 AI 智能体在实务工作上的追赶速度有多快。大约一年前该基准发布时，当时最强的系统 Manus 只完成了 2.5% 的任务。如今 Fable 5.2 完成的专业工作数量已是那时的 16 倍多。

inlines.text: 这一进展说明 AI 智能体在实务工作上的追赶速度有多快。大约一年前该基准发布时，当时最强的系统 Manus 只完成了 2.5% 的任务。如今 Fable 5.2 完成的专业工作数量已是那时的 16 倍多。

blocks.text: 与最近的测量结果相比，这次提升同样很大。今年 7 月，同系列的旧模型 Fable 5 还以约 16% 领先。那个分数本身已是重大进步：最好的智能体在八个月内把以专业质量完成的工作比例提高到了原来的四倍以上。四个月后，Fable 5.2 达到 41.3%，约为 Fable 5 七月成绩的 2.5 倍。它的上一代模型 Fable 5.1 也远远落后，仅略低于 18%，而 Fable 5.2 完成的工作量是它的两倍多。

blocks.text: 当前排行榜的接下来两位是 Anthropic 的 Opus 5.5，为 21.25%，以及 OpenAI 的 GPT 6 Astra，为 20.83%。Fable 5.2 的成功率几乎是市场上次优系统的两倍。谷歌在测试中最强的模型 Gemini Argon 4 以 17.08% 排在第五，而 GPT-5.2、Gemini 3 Pro 等旧模型则低于 3%。

blocks.text: Fable 5.2 在 3D 模型、音频和建筑领域取得突破

blocks.text: Fable 5.2 成功完成的任务中，有近 50 项是测试中此前没有任何 AI 智能体解决过的。Scale Labs 表示，AI 在其他任务上仍几乎无能为力，尤其是工业产品设计和动画。研究人员称，AI 智能体在测试中失败时，通常交付的是业余水准的作品、不完整的结果、损坏的文件或自相矛盾的设计。

blocks.text: 价值 14.4 万美元的真实工作

inlines.text: 价值 14.4 万美元的真实工作

blocks.text: 传统 AI 测试往往只考察孤立技能，而RLI 研究论文覆盖的是完整的工作任务。数据集包含 Upwork 平台上 358 位经过认证的专业人士完成的 240 个项目，这些工作总价值约 14.4 万美元。

blocks.text: 单个项目平均花费 632.60 美元，人类自由职业者平均需要近 29 小时完成。任务范围从视频剪辑到 CAD 设计、游戏开发和数据分析。为了完成这些工作，AI 智能体可以使用一个虚拟工作区，里面有 Blender、GIMP、Audacity 等常用专业软件，以及用于图像、音频和视频生成的专门 AI 工具。

blocks.text: 由人类专家接受培训后人工核查 AI 智能体是否成功完成任务。他们会用相关专业软件打开提交的文件，把 AI 的输出与人类自由职业者的交付成果直接对比。CAIS 尝试用另一个 AI 来自动完成这项劳动密集的审核工作，但迄今未能成功。原因是 AI 审核员自己几乎不会操作这些专业软件，容易被表面光鲜、技术上却有缺陷的提交内容蒙骗，给模型打分也过于宽松。

blocks.text: Anthropic's new model Fable 5.2 makes a massive leap on the Remote Labor Index, completing more than 41 percent of real freelance projects at professional quality. The system leaves both its direct predecessor and the entire competition far behind.

inlines.text: Anthropic's new model Fable 5.2 makes a massive leap on the Remote Labor Index, completing more than 41 percent of real freelance projects at professional quality. The system leaves both its direct predecessor and the entire competition far behind.

blocks.text: On the Remote Labor Index (RLI) from Scale Labs and the Center for AI Safety (CAIS), Anthropic's new model Fable 5.2 takes the lead with 41.3 percent. The test measures how often AI agents complete real freelance jobs well enough for a paying client to accept the work.

inlines.text: On the
Remote Labor Index (RLI)

from Scale Labs and the Center for AI Safety (CAIS), Anthropic's new model Fable 5.2 takes the lead with 41.3 percent. The test measures how often AI agents complete real freelance jobs well enough for a paying client to accept the work.

blocks.text: The progress shows how fast AI agents are catching up on practical work. When the benchmark launched about a year ago, the top system at the time, Manus, managed just 2.5 percent of tasks. Fable 5.2 now completes more than 16 times as many professional jobs.

inlines.text: The progress shows how fast AI agents are catching up on practical work. When the benchmark launched about a year ago, the top system at the time, Manus, managed just 2.5 percent of tasks. Fable 5.2 now completes more than 16 times as many professional jobs.

blocks.text: The jump is also large compared to the most recent measurements. In July, Fable 5, an older model from the same family, was still in front at about 16 percent. That score was already a big step forward: the best agents had more than quadrupled the share of jobs they completed at professional quality within eight months. Four months later, Fable 5.2 hits 41.3 percent. That's roughly two and a half times Fable 5's July score. Its direct predecessor, Fable 5.1, also trails far behind at just under 18 percent, and Fable 5.2 completes more than twice as many jobs.

blocks.text: The next spots on the current leaderboard go to Anthropic's Opus 5.5 at 21.25 percent and OpenAI's GPT 6 Astra at 20.83 percent. Fable 5.2 works almost twice as successfully as the next-best systems on the market. Google's strongest model in the test, Gemini Argon 4, lands in fifth place at 17.08 percent, while older models like GPT-5.2 or Gemini 3 Pro sit below three percent.

blocks.text: Fable 5.2 breaks through in 3D models, audio, and architecture

inlines.text: Fable 5.2 breaks through in 3D models, audio, and architecture

blocks.text: Scale Labs said on X that Fable 5.2 makes its biggest gains in editing audio and music, designing architecture and interior spaces, and creating 3D models. The agent also handles long, complex projects that previously top-ranked models regularly failed.

inlines.text: Scale Labs said on X

that Fable 5.2 makes its biggest gains in editing audio and music, designing architecture and interior spaces, and creating 3D models. The agent also handles long, complex projects that previously top-ranked models regularly failed.

blocks.text: Nearly 50 of Fable 5.2's successful completions were jobs no AI agent in the test had solved before. Scale Labs says the AI can still barely handle other tasks, especially industrial product design and animations. When AI agents fail in the test, they typically deliver amateur-quality work, incomplete results, broken files, or contradictory designs, according to the researchers.

blocks.text: Real jobs worth $144,000

inlines.text: Real jobs worth $144,000

blocks.text: Unlike conventional AI tests that often check only isolated skills, the RLI research paper covers complete work assignments. The dataset includes 240 completed projects from 358 verified professionals on the Upwork platform. Together, these jobs are worth about $144,000.

inlines.text: Unlike conventional AI tests that often check only isolated skills, the
RLI research paper
covers complete work assignments. The dataset includes 240 completed projects from 358 verified professionals on the Upwork platform. Together, these jobs are worth about $144,000.

blocks.text: A single project costs an average of $632.60 and takes a human freelancer an average of just under 29 hours. Tasks range from video editing to CAD design, game development, and data analysis. To work on these jobs, AI agents get access to a virtual workspace with common professional software like Blender, GIMP, or Audacity, along with specialized AI tools for image, audio, and video generation.

blocks.text: Trained human experts manually check whether an AI agent completed a job successfully. They open the submitted files in the relevant professional software and compare the AI's output directly with the work the human freelancer delivered. CAIS's attempts to automate this labor-intensive review with another AI have so far failed. Because AI reviewers can barely operate the professional software themselves, they're fooled by submissions that look polished on the surface but are technically flawed, and they rate the models far too generously.
